tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

# Task brief (verbatim obligations, as given by the user)

Normative hierarchy: Charter v0 highest (contradictions reported, never resolved); spec specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.md validated and frozen, cite by section; draft branches formal/* are material only (reuse when matching the spec, divergences resolved in favor of the spec and listed).
Layout (suggested): Ern/MemoryModel/Machine.lean (Part III), Ern/MemoryModel/Access/*.lean (Parts IV-XIII, XV-XVI), Ern/MemoryModel/Arena.lean (Part XIV: arenas as reference library abstraction; O17-O19 derived over O1-O16 plus metadata; ArenaInv and the §56 guard as abstraction contract), Ern/MemoryModel/Refinement.lean (§82), Ern/Lib/HandlePool.lean, Ern/Lib/DataStack.lean (non-normative), test modules imported by no model module. MM-01 (Part II) referenced, not a module.

Obligations (all mandatory):
1. Machine (Part III). Relations total and deterministic; interpreters calculable with static obligations and WF as proof arguments; agreement theorems both ways on their domain; admissible-state invariants preserved; P1-P4, no double free, frame lemmas, read-after-write on every included sub-range (§16).
2. Kernel (Parts IV-XIII). Every operation exactly as written, including §63.8 and §77 local self-blocking prevention, §65 store rules (derived authority, free leaf, arrival-state exercisability), §72 parameter-origin rule, §73 reanchoring to the first surviving active origin, §69/§70 end of use and free, pinning rules. Locals created by entering a frame are owned directly by the frame; alloc creates exactly one root. Theorems: preservation of WF3 ∧ Inv3 ∧ AnchorOrderHeld ∧ NoOrphan by every step; reachable invariant from S3.init statics under DDSound; exitFrame_no_dangling; call_params_effective_protected; effective_exclusive; init_only_by_writes, init_statics, and the global induction (every Init leaf of a reached state was declared or written); correspondence between Step and Reachable.
3. Arena (Part XIV). issue_as_kernel, reset_as_kernel (both directions, same arrival state on the kernel part), newArena_as_library (no safety property depends on the guard), arena_reuse_safe, ArenaInv preserved.
4. Refinement (§82). Repr including MM-02 WF; R1, R2, R4, R6 for every kernel operation and derived arena operation; simulation with parameters fixed once per run; freeSound_derived; pinned_address_stable; exclusive_bytes. Decisions to apply: declared disjointness is disjointness of leaves (byte disjointness follows from layout well-formedness); a pointer to an empty region has address = base of the effective anchor's allocation and that allocation as provenance; a region's pointer address is the lowest address among its non-empty leaves; a leaf receiving a reference has pointer size (stated hypothesis, classed types/ABI).
5. HandlePool (contract: v0.4 annex). Composite borrow (companion derived from internal over the whole storage, entries derived from the companion); resolveMany Observe by Observe derivations, distinctness only in Modify; allocSlot/freeSlot require a live pool and Modify on the pool value; newPool requires Uninit storage; freeSlot ends the entry content with endUse effects, preconditions excluding internal and its ancestors; PoolInv = entry disjointness + pool_no_stale_access + transition guarantee that freeSlot never succeeds on an entry covered by an active companion descendant. Theorems: pool_resolve_modify_exclusive, pool_no_stale_access, stale/other-pool/atomicity/distinctness, pool_freeSlot_ends_content under the Modify right.
6. DataStack (contract below, identifier DS-v1). Marks carry stack identity and a fresh mark identifier; the stack keeps the ordered list of live marks; rewind m fails on a dead or foreign mark, rejects if an active authority derived from internal covers a cell above m, otherwise returns those cells to available and removes m and every mark above it; push and grow use the derived issue; grow is in place only (same base, extension into the space directly after the block, fail otherwise). Theorems: rewind_rejects_live_above, mark_no_aba (for every removed mark), rewind_keeps_older_marks, grow_same_base, grow_keeps_prefix_init, grow_keeps_prefix_bytes through the refinement.
7. Corpora. Encode MM2-H (first execution), MM3-H and MM23-H (replay) from the attached material, plus new cases: §63.8 and §77 self-blocking (reject, with twins), §56 guard, corrected HandlePool, DataStack (including ABA and a multi-stack frame scenario), W1-W3. Each case: reached state from the initial state, expected verdict from its source, positive twin for each rejection, class. MM23-H15 and H16 must now pass. Section J of MM3-H stays unencoded and classified. No case is corrected or bypassed.

Docstrings: model modules: every def/theorem cites the specification clause it formalizes. Library modules: cite the applicable spec clauses (§36, §56, ...) and the local contract identifier (HandlePool v0.4 annex, DS-v1), stated as non-normative.
Exclusions: instrumented checked variants; duplicate _pre statements; references to draft reports; concurrency beyond the stat boundary; syntax.
Rules: zero sorry; #print axioms at most {propext, Quot.sound} on every constant (checked by script); no noncomputable; lake build without warnings; nothing invented - a clause that cannot be formalized as written is reported, not interpreted; no statement weakened relative to its clause; adversarial review rounds, every finding re-checked by a refuter.
Opening the PR: only if every mandatory obligation is proved and every expected/obtained mismatch resolved; otherwise commit on the branch, do not push, do not open the PR, end with a blocking report (each unproved obligation or mismatch classified as specification defect, module defect or case defect, with its counterexample). Never present a partial formalization as conforming.

182	**Criterion for "conditional".** An obligation is conditional when its theorem is proved only under hypotheses that are either not spec clauses (`PtrDecided`, `StepObl`) or §55/§57 invariants imposed on states that library runs reach without them (B2, B3). Since `6610252` no obligation depends on `KAux`. This applies to O3.a and O3.b (`KInv` and `ArenaInv`), O4.e (per-state WF3 ∧ NoDangling, `StepObl`) and O5.g (`KInv` at each `PReachI` step). O2.d (`exitFrame_no_dangling` on WF3 ∧ I1 ∧ NoDangling), O4.b (`Repr` ∧ WF3) and O4.f (`Repr` ∧ WF3 ∧ NoDangling) are per-step lemmas whose hypothesis is the pre-state invariant; they count as proved because the brief names them as per-step properties. The D.3 reconstruction part of O5.d (`contentEnd_preserves`, `KInv` to `KInv`) has the per-step form of `op_preserves` (O2.b) and counts as proved for the same reason. O3.a and O3.b are per-step too, and their hypotheses are also spec invariants. They count as conditional because `R/map/arena.md` C4 asks for "`issue_as_kernel` without extra hypotheses", and `ArenaInv` is false on a library-reachable state with a live entry (B3). This line is a reporting choice, not a spec rule. Under a uniform per-step criterion O3.a and O3.b would count as proved; under a uniform reachable-state criterion O2.d, O4.b, O4.f and O5.d would also be conditional (B2).

182	**Criterion for "conditional".** An obligation is conditional when its theorem is proved only under hypotheses that are either not spec clauses (`PtrDecided`, `StepObl`) or §55/§57 invariants imposed on states that library runs reach without them (B2, B3). Since `6610252` no obligation depends on `KAux`. This applies to O3.a and O3.b (`KInv` and `ArenaInv`), O4.e (per-state WF3 ∧ NoDangling, `StepObl`) and O5.g (`KInv` at each `PReachI` step). O2.d (`exitFrame_no_dangling` on WF3 ∧ I1 ∧ NoDangling), O4.b (`Repr` ∧ WF3) and O4.f (`Repr` ∧ WF3 ∧ NoDangling) are per-step lemmas whose hypothesis is the pre-state invariant; they count as proved because the brief names them as per-step properties. The D.3 reconstruction part of O5.d (`contentEnd_preserves`, `KInv` to `KInv`) has the per-step form of `op_preserves` (O2.b) and counts as proved for the same reason. O3.a and O3.b are per-step too, and their hypotheses are also spec invariants. They count as conditional because `R/map/arena.md` C4 asks for "`issue_as_kernel` without extra hypotheses", and `ArenaInv` is false on a library-reachable state with a live entry (B3). This line is a reporting choice, not a spec rule. Under a uniform per-step criterion O3.a and O3.b would count as proved; under a uniform reachable-state criterion O2.d, O4.b, O4.f and O5.d would also be conditional (B2).

intro i st' h
  rcases getElem?_set_cases h with ⟨rfl, rfl⟩ | ⟨-, h⟩
  · exact ⟨st₀, hst, hi, hc⟩
  · exact ⟨st', h, rfl, rfl⟩

/-- Every library step keeps `StackShape` (DS-v1, non-normative; §76.2, §76.3 at `newStack`,
§42 afterwards). -/
theorem DStep.stackShape {k : K} {D D' : DState} (h : DStep k D D') (hw : StackShape D) :
    StackShape D' := by
  have hA := h.akeep
  cases h with
  | kernel => exact stackShape_keep hA hw fun i st' h => ⟨st', h, rfl, rfl⟩
  | @newStack _ _ _ int hs =>
    obtain ⟨hp, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hs
    intro i st' h
    rcases getElem?_append_single h with h | rfl
    · exact hw i st' h
    · have hi := hp.base.internalAuth
      cases hy : D.kern.A[int]? with
      | none => rw [hy] at hi; exact hi.elim
      | some y =>
        rw [hy] at hi
        refine ⟨y, hy, hi.2, fun c hc => ?_⟩
        have := hp.base.fpSup c hc; simpa [S3.afp, hy] using this
  | push hs => cases hs with | ok hst => exact stackShape_keep hA hw (set_keeps hst rfl rfl)
  | mark hs => cases hs with | ok hst => exact stackShape_keep hA hw (set_keeps hst rfl rfl)
  | rewind hs => cases hs with | ok hst => exact stackShape_keep hA hw (set_keeps hst rfl rfl)
  | grow hs => cases hs with | ok hst => exact stackShape_keep hA hw (set_keeps hst rfl rfl)

/-- Every library-reachable state satisfies `StackShape` (DS-v1, non-normative; §47: no stack
initially; §76.2, §76.3, §42). -/
theorem DReach.stackShape {k : K} {statics : Statics} {D : DState} (h : DReach k statics D) :
    StackShape D := by
  induction h with
  | init => intro i st h; simp [DState.init] at h
  | step _ hs ih => exact hs.stackShape ih

/-- The authority added by `split` of `src` on one region can be released at once (support for
DS-v1, non-normative, `rewind`; §62): it is active, derived, held by the current frame (§62.1,
§62.2), has no descendant (§62.3: origins precede, §42) and, under `DBound`, anchors no place
(§62.3, §62.4). -/
theorem release_after_split {s : S3} {src : Nat} {R : List Nat} (hb : DBound s) :
    ReleasePre (splitEff s src [R]) s.A.length := by
  have hy₀ := split_block s src R
  refine ⟨⟨_, hy₀, rfl⟩, by rw [hy₀]; simp [OptP], by rw [hy₀]; exact rfl,
    fun j hj hn => ?_, fun q _ _ hx => absurd (hb q _ hx) (Nat.lt_irrefl _)⟩
  have := chain_lt hn
  have := List.mem_range.1 hj; simp [splitEff] at this; omega

/-- `rewind_ok_iff` (DS-v1, non-normative: "rewind m fails on a dead or foreign mark, rejects if an
active authority derived from internal covers a cell above m, otherwise returns those cells to
available"; §36; §61.1, §61.3, §62 through Part XIV). On a library-reachable state (`DReach`, a
state invariant), for an existing stack, `rewind m` is `ok` exactly when `m` is a live mark of the
stack (DS-v1), the administrative right of §36 holds (`AdminRight`), and no active authority
derived from `internal` covers a cell above `m` (DS-v1). The model has no explicit check of the
last condition: it is the effective `Modify` of `internal` required by `split` (§61.1, with the
effective mode of §43). The other checks of `split` and `release` never reject there: `internal`
has own mode `Modify` and covers the cells (`DReach.stackShape`, §76.2, §76.3), and anchors name
existing authorities (`dBound_of_reachable`). DS-v1 does not list §36: on the reachable state of
`Witness.reading_rewind_right` every DS-v1 condition for success holds and §36 rejects (the §61.1
check of `split` fails there too). -/
theorem rewind_ok_iff {k : K} {statics : Statics} {D : DState} (hr : DReach k statics D)
    {j : Nat} {st : Stack} (hst : D.stacks[j]? = some st) {m : Mark} :
    (∃ D', RewindStep k j m D (.ok D')) ↔
      LiveMark j st m ∧ AdminRight D.kern st ∧
        ∀ (x l : Nat) (y : Authority), D.kern.A[x]? = some y → y.active = true →
          st.internal ∈ D.kern.ancs x → l ∈ y.footprint → l ∉ above st m := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨D', h⟩
    cases h with
    | ok h hm ha hsp =>
      rw [hst] at h; cases h
      have hp := (Guarded.ok_iff.1 hsp).1
      exact ⟨hm, ha, fun x l y hy ya hx hly hl =>
        no_desc_of_modify hy ya hly hx (hp.modifyOn _ (List.mem_singleton_self _) l hl)⟩
  · rintro ⟨hm, ha, hno⟩
    obtain ⟨yi, hyi, hmi, hci⟩ := hr.stackShape j st hst
    have yia : yi.active = true := by
      obtain ⟨y, hy, ya⟩ := ha.1; rw [hyi] at hy; cases hy; exact ya
    have hab : ∀ l ∈ above st m, l ∈ yi.footprint :=
      fun l hl => hci l (List.mem_of_mem_drop (List.mem_of_mem_take hl))
    have hmod : ∀ l ∈ above st m, effective D.kern st.internal l = some .modify := by
      intro l hl
      have hd : descModes D.kern st.internal l = [] := by
        apply nil_of_forall_not_mem; intro e he
        obtain ⟨x, y, hy, ya, hly, hx, -⟩ := mem_descModes.1 he
        exact hno x l y hy ya hx hly hl
      rw [effective_eq hyi yia (hab l hl), hd]; simp [effOf, hmi]
    have hex : D.kern.ExercisableAt st.internal .modify := by
      have hmr := ha.2
      simp only [MetaRight, arenaValue, Stack.entry, hyi] at hmr
      cases hv : yi.holder with
      | frame f => rw [hv] at hmr; exact hmr.elim
      | place v =>
        rw [hv] at hmr
        obtain ⟨b, -, hb, hall⟩ := hmr
        exact .held hyi yia (.inr hmi) hv hb hall
    have hsp : SplitPre k D.kern st.internal [above st m] := by
      refine ⟨ha.1, hex, fun r hr p hp => ?_, fun r hr p hp => ?_, List.pairwise_singleton _ _,
        fun r hr p hp x _ hd => ?_⟩
      · rw [List.mem_singleton.1 hr] at hp; exact hmod p hp

# Readings — datastack (DS-v1, non-normative; spec v0 §36, §38, §46, §47, §56, §58, Part XIV, §82)

Module: `formal/Ern/Lib/DataStack.lean` (namespace `Ern.Lib.DataStack`).
Machine-checked examples: section `Witness` of that module (`run_ok`, `reading_above`,
`reading_order`, `reading_mark`, `reading_grow_dst`, `reading_newStack`, `reading_rewind_right`,
all by `decide` on library-reachable states under `Access.Examples.K0`). Two examples are scratch
files outside the repository, re-elaborated against `b4a5cd3`: `../final5/nostack.lean` (DS-R3) and
`../final5/d17.lean` (DS-R13).

Source of the contract: the brief's obligation 6 (DS-v1). Spec v0 does not define it (Part XIV
preamble: "The contracts of `HandlePool` and `DataStack` belong to their library abstractions and
are not defined here"). Every entry: clause, reading used, alternative, example whose verdict
changes. "[draft]" = the reading of the draft (`formal/derivability_0.1`, `Lib/DataStack.lean`),
used per policy ("use the draft's reading if the draft matches one of the readings").

## Readings that change verdicts

**DS-R3 "foreign" mark.** Reading: a mark is live for stack `j` iff `m.stack = j ∧ m ∈ st.marks`
(`LiveMark`); the stack identity is checked explicitly although, under `MarksWF` (proved on every
library-reachable state), membership alone implies it. The explicit identity check changes no verdict
on reachable states.
`rewind` on a stack index that does not exist is `reject` (no stack value) [draft]. This is a reason
to reject that DS-v1 does not list (narrow check ds4-2). Alternative: a mark of a stack that does not
exist is not live, so DS-v1's "fails on a dead or foreign mark" gives `fail`; or DS-v1 is silent.
Example (`../final5/nostack.lean`): on the initial state `d0` (`DReach.init`, no stack),
`rewind(0, ⟨0,0,0⟩)` is `reject` through `RewindStep.noStack` and neither `ok` nor `fail`; `fail` under
the alternative.

**DS-R6 order inside `grow`.** The derived issue's static checks (`IssueStatic`) cannot be read on
the state before the release of `b` (the destination still holds `b`, §77.2 "holding no active
authority"). Reading: block lookup and `0 < extra` (`reject`); `release(b)` (`reject` if refused);
`IssueStatic` on the released state (`reject`); `InPlace` (`fail`, the state unchanged); `split`;
`store`. Alternative: in-place `fail` before the release. Changes the verdict when `b` cannot be
released and the block is not in place (`reject` here, `fail` under the alternative).

**DS-R7 `push` without room: `fail` [draft].** DS-v1 says only that `push` uses the derived issue.
Reading: the `size` cells at the top must exist (`top + size ≤ |cells|`); otherwise `fail`
(availability, §77.4), checked after `IssueStatic` on the requested cells that exist. Alternative:
"region belongs to the administered storage" (§77.2, static) gives `reject`. Example
(`Witness.reading_order` (3)): `push(0, 3, 4)` on a stack of 2 cells is `fail`.

**DS-R8 `push` static checks are those of the derived issue (`Arena.IssueStatic`, §77.1, §77.2).**
Not the draft's restricted ones: an `Init` destination is not rejected (spec v0 §77.2, O8.2).
`push` of size 0 is accepted (issue of the empty region): the empty block blocks no `rewind`, and
`rewind` forgets it in the metadata while its authority stays active [draft DS-3].

**DS-R9 `newStack` preconditions: §76.5 applies [draft]** (was R5; review round 2, DS-1). DS-v1
alternative, the static checks of the derived issue (`IssueStatic`) and `store(6, 5)` are `ok` on
the same released and split state, and authority 6 is held by place 5.

**DS-R12 reasons for which `rewind` rejects: §36 applies** (B47). DS-v1: "rewind m fails on a
dead or foreign mark, rejects if an active authority derived from internal covers a cell above m,
otherwise returns those cells to available and removes m and every mark above it". It names one
reason to reject. Reading: §36 applies too (normative: `MetaRight` requires `Modify` exercisable on
the stack value; the abstraction adds no rights to the kernel), so `rewind` rejects without
`AdminRight`. On library-reachable states and for an existing stack, this is the only reason outside
DS-v1's list (`rewind_ok_iff`, R3). A stack index with no stack gives `reject` for another reason
outside the list, `RewindStep.noStack` (DS-R3). Alternative: DS-v1's list is exhaustive, so
`rewind` is `ok` whenever the mark is live and no such authority covers a cell above it. Example (`Witness.reading_rewind_right`,
decided): `d16` is reached by the rewind to `⟨0,1,1⟩`, the program's `release(5)` and a callee frame
with no parameter or local. There, mark `⟨0,0,0⟩` is live for stack 0 and no active authority
derived from `internal` 4 covers cell 2, the cell above it. `rewind ⟨0,0,0⟩` is `reject` here and
`ok` under the alternative. The kernel sequence cannot realize the alternative: `split` of
`internal` also rejects in `d16`, because `internal` is not exercisable at `Modify` (§61.1).
`AdminRight` has two conjuncts. `d16` tests only `MetaRight` (`internal` is active there); the other
conjunct, `internal` active, is DS-R13.

**DS-R13 a live mark of a dead stack** (narrow check ds4-3). DS-v1: "the stack keeps the ordered list
of live marks; rewind m fails on a dead or foreign mark". It does not speak of a dead stack. §46:
"The arena is **live** if `internal` is active", read for a stack by `AdminRight`. Reading: the
liveness of the stack is part of the §36 check (`AdminRight`: `internal` active), so `rewind` is
`reject` (`RewindStep.static`). Alternative 1: DS-v1's list is exhaustive (the DS-R12 alternative):
`ok`. Alternative 2: a mark of a dead stack is a dead mark: `fail` (under the DS-R2 order the mark is
checked first). Example (`../final5/d17.lean`: `d17_facts`, `d17_only_reject`): `d17` is `d11` (the
rewind to `⟨0,1,1⟩` and the program's `release(5)`) followed by the program's `release(4)` of
`internal` 4. Mark `⟨0,0,0⟩` is live for stack 0, no active authority derived from `internal` covers
cell 2, `MetaRight` still holds and `internal` is inactive. `rewind ⟨0,0,0⟩` is `reject` and nothing
else here, `ok` under alternative 1 and `fail` under alternative 2.

## Readings that change no accepted program (representation)

- **R1 State.** `DState = ⟨kern, stacks, fresh⟩`, separate from `S3` (§38, §46); a stack is its
  registry index, stacks are never removed; `fresh` is a global counter (§9 "a monotonically
  increasing counter is one possible representation"). The arena registry is not in `DState`: the
  guard reads it through the parameter `others` (§56), as `Arena.NewArenaPre` reads stacks through
  its `others`.
- **R2 Available cells** = positions `≥ top` of the ordered cells (`Stack.entry.available =
  cells.drop top`); `push` and `grow` take cells at the top only and `rewind` returns exactly
  `above`, so this is a set of leaves as in §46.
- **R3 `rewind` kernel part [draft]:** the derived reset of Part XIV restricted to `above st m`:
  `split(internal, [above])` then `release` of the new authority. Plus an explicit §36 check
  (`AdminRight`: `internal` active and `MetaRight` on the stack value) before the split, like
  `IssueStatic.live/metaRight`. **Exact outcome, proved** (`rewind_ok_iff`, hypothesis: the state
  invariant `DReach` only, no `KInv`, no I3): for an existing stack, `rewind m` is `ok` iff `m` is
  live for the stack (DS-v1), `AdminRight` holds (§36), and no active authority derived from
  `internal` covers a cell of `above st m` (DS-v1). The model does not check the DS-v1 condition
  explicitly. It is the effective `Modify` of `internal` that `split` requires (§61.1, effective
  mode of §43; §61.3 follows). No other check of `split` or `release` rejects on such a state:
  - `internal` has own mode `Modify` and covers the cells (`DReach.stackShape`: §76.2 and §76.3 at
    `newStack`, kept by every step since modes and footprints never change, §42);
  - every anchor names an existing authority (`dBound_of_reachable`), so the fresh authority
    anchors no place (§62.3, §62.4).

  For an existing stack, the only rejection outside DS-v1's list is §36 (DS-R12, DS-R13); a missing
  stack gives `reject` through `noStack` (DS-R3). Not proved here: whether the explicit
  §36 check ever rejects when the `split` check of §61.1 (`internal` active and exercisable at
  `Modify`) would accept.
- **R4 "removes m and every mark above it":** "above" = later in the ordered list;
  `marks := takeWhile (· ≠ m)`. Blocks with base `≥ m.top` are forgotten [draft].
- **R5, R6, R7:** moved to DS-R9, DS-R10, DS-R11 above (they change verdicts or arrival states;
  review round 2, DS-1).
- **R8 Library runs:** `DStep.kernel` admits any kernel step of non-administrative code.

Fixed during the final check (module defects found by the report check, section 9; each fix went through a narrow refuter check, section 9):
- **B45, fixed in `6610252`** (O5.d). The D.3 reconstruction obligation ("la correspondance des effets et la préservation des invariants sous ce droit constituent une **obligation explicite de reconstruction**") no longer needs `KAux`.
  - `Lib.HandlePool.contentEnd_preserves` (Lib/HandlePool.lean:559) takes `KInv` and `ContentEndPre` and gives `KInv`. `freeSlot_preserves` (:1791) has the same shape.
  - `KAux` is preserved separately by `contentEnd_preserves_kAux` (:584) and `freeSlot_preserves_kAux` (:1798). The statement of `xreach_inv` (:704) is unchanged.
  - `contentEnd_noDangling` (:515) now takes `I1 s` instead of `RootHeldConv s`, the same swap that `a14dda0` made in the kernel's `EndFree.endUse_noDangling`. On its own the swap is not a strengthening: the two hypotheses are incomparable, as for the kernel (`R/reports/fix1-kernel.md`). `R/recheck4/refute/full.lean` (`full_old_domain_not_new`) gives a state `sib` with `WF3`, `NoDangling`, `RootHeldConv`, `ContentEndPre K0 sib 4 2` and `WF3` of the arrival state, but `¬ I1 sib`.
  - Under `KInv` nothing is lost. `I1` is a conjunct of `KInv`, and the only caller, `contentEnd_preserves`, passes it. `R/recheck4/oldforms.lean` re-derives the `6e56758` forms of `contentEnd_preserves` and `freeSlot_preserves` (`KInv ∧ KAux` to `KInv ∧ KAux`) from the new pairs, so those two statements are stronger than before (narrow check, pool4-1).
- **B47, resolved in `b4a5cd3` by a theorem and two readings** (O6).
  - `Lib.DataStack.rewind_ok_iff` (Lib/DataStack.lean:661). On a library-reachable state (`DReach`, the only invariant used: no `KInv`, I3 or `KAux`) and for an existing stack (`D.stacks[j]? = some st`), `rewind m` is `ok` iff `m` is live for the stack (`LiveMark`, DS-v1), `AdminRight` holds (§36), and no active authority derived from `internal` covers a cell of `above st m` (DS-v1). The model has no explicit check of the last condition: it is the effective `Modify` of `internal` that `split` requires (§61.1). Supporting results: `DReach.stackShape` (:631) and `dBound_of_reachable` (:546).
  - What remains is a contract question, not a module defect: `rewind` rejects for two reasons that DS-v1's list does not contain.
  - §36 (`AdminRight`). `Witness.reading_rewind_right` (:1280), on `d16` (:1271): every DS-v1 condition for `ok` holds, the callee has no right on the stack value, and `rewind` is `reject`; it is `ok` under the reading that DS-v1's list is exhaustive (DS-R12, Q27). The other conjunct of `AdminRight`, `internal` active, rejects a live mark of a dead stack, where a third reading gives `fail` (DS-R13, Q28; narrow check, ds4-3).
  - A missing stack. `RewindStep.noStack` (:218) gives `reject` on the initial state, a library-reachable state (`R/final5/nostack.lean`). DS-v1 gives `fail` if a mark of a stack that does not exist counts as dead or foreign, and is otherwise silent. DS-R12 is therefore restricted to existing stacks, and DS-R3 records this case (narrow check, ds4-2; submitted with Q23).

import Ern.Lib.DataStack

open Ern.MemoryModel Ern.MemoryModel.Access Ern.MemoryModel.Arena Ern.Lib.DataStack
open Ern.Lib.DataStack.Witness Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Examples

def d17 : DState := ⟨releaseEff d11.kern 4, d11.stacks, d11.fresh⟩

theorem d17_facts :
    DReach K0 wst d17 ∧ d17.stacks[0]? = some st9 ∧ LiveMark 0 st9 m0 ∧
    ¬ d17.kern.Active st9.internal ∧ MetaRight d17.kern st9.entry ∧
    (∀ x ∈ List.range d17.kern.A.length, OptP (d17.kern.A[x]?) (fun y => y.active = true →
      st9.internal ∈ d17.kern.ancs x → ∀ l ∈ above st9 m0, l ∉ y.footprint) True) ∧
    ¬ AdminRight d17.kern st9 ∧ RewindStep K0 0 m0 d17 .reject := by
  have r11 : DReach K0 wst d11 := .step d9_reach (.kernel (.release (.ok (by decide))))
  have r17 : DReach K0 wst d17 := .step r11 (.kernel (.release (.ok (by decide))))
  exact ⟨r17, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide,
    .static (st := st9) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide)⟩

-- the outcome is only reject: no fail, no ok
theorem d17_only_reject : ∀ o, RewindStep K0 0 m0 d17 o → o = .reject := by
  intro o h
  cases h with
  | noStack h => rfl
  | dead h hm => exact absurd (by decide : LiveMark 0 st9 m0) (by
      have : d17.stacks[0]? = some st9 := by decide
      rw [this] at h; cases h; exact hm)
  | static => rfl
  | split => rfl
  | release => rfl
  | ok h hm ha => exact absurd ha (by
      have : d17.stacks[0]? = some st9 := by decide
      rw [this] at h; cases h; decide)

example : above st9 m0 = [2] := by decide

-- initial (reachable) state: no stack; rewind 0 m0 rejects via noStack, never ok, never fail
example : DReach Examples.K0 wst d0 ∧ RewindStep Examples.K0 0 m0 d0 .reject ∧
    (¬ ∃ D', RewindStep Examples.K0 0 m0 d0 (.ok D')) ∧ ¬ RewindStep Examples.K0 0 m0 d0 .fail := by

/-- The end of the content preserves `NoDangling` (§54, §69; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3), under
`WF3` (§49) and `I1` (§50): an active authority on a leaf of a place that stops being usable is
derived, and blocked by §69.2 on dying storage, or a root, held by the owner of the root place of
the leaf (`rootHeldConv_active`), which stays usable. -/
theorem contentEnd_noDangling {k : K} {s : S3} {q i : Nat} (hw : WF3 s) (hnd : NoDangling s)
    (h1 : I1 s) (hpre : ContentEndPre k s q i) (hw' : WF3 (endUseEff s q)) :
    NoDangling (endUseEff s q) := by
  have hU := EndFree.cleanup_usable (endUseS s q)
  intro j z hz za q' hq l hl hlz
  obtain ⟨hz₀, hnh, hlive⟩ := EndFree.endUse_active hz za
  by_cases hq₀ : ¬ s.Usable q'
  · exact hnd j z hz₀ za q' hq₀ l hl hlz
  replace hq₀ := Decidable.of_not_not hq₀
  obtain ⟨-, hleaf, hlq⟩ := mem_footprint.1 hl
  have hl₀ : s.Usable l := usable_of_partOf hw (l + 1) l q' (Nat.lt_succ_self l) hlq hq₀
  have hl₁ : ¬ (endUseS s q).Usable l := fun hu => hq (usable_of_part hw' hlq ((hU l).2 hu))
  cases hzo : z.origin with
  | some o =>
    have hacc := hpre.dying j (List.mem_range.2 (lt_of_getElem? hz₀))
    unfold DyingAccessOK OptP at hacc; rw [hz₀] at hacc
    rcases hacc za (by rw [hzo]; simp) ⟨l, hlz, hleaf, hl₀, hl₁⟩ with e | e
    · exact hnh e
    · exact e hlive
  | none =>
    obtain ⟨-, -, r, -, -, -, hr, hlr, -⟩ := hw.rootChain j z l hz₀ hlz hleaf
    obtain ⟨pr, hpr, hh⟩ := rootHeldConv_active hw h1 hnd j z l r hz₀ za hzo hlz hr hlr
    have hnown : ¬ OwnedIn s.P q r := fun hown => by
      cases hown with
      | @direct _ o _ hpl ho hpart =>
        have e : pr.owner = .place o := by rw [hpr] at hpl; cases hpl; exact ho
        rw [hh, e] at hnh; exact hnh hpart
      | @step _ o _ hpl ho hown' =>
        have e : pr.owner = .place o := by rw [hpr] at hpl; cases hpl; exact ho
        rw [hh, e] at hlive
        have := EndFree.dead_false hlive
        simp only [endUseS, Bool.or_eq_false_iff, decide_eq_false_iff_not] at this
        exact this.2 hown'
    have hd : (endUseS s q).dead r = false := by
      simp only [endUseS, ← hw.deadOf hlr, EndFree.dead_false hl₀, Bool.false_or,
        decide_eq_false_iff_not]
      exact hnown
    have hr₁ : (endUseS s q).Usable r := EndFree.usable_of_owner hpr hd (hh ▸ hlive)
    exact hl₁ ((hU l).1 (usable_of_partOf hw' (l + 1) l r (Nat.lt_succ_self l) hlr ((hU r).2 hr₁)))

/-- The end of the content of a slot place `q` under `ContentEndPre` preserves the kernel invariant
`KInv` (§57) (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3: "la correspondance des effets et la préservation des
invariants sous ce droit constituent une obligation explicite de reconstruction"; §69 effect); the auxiliary `KAux` is preserved by
`contentEnd_preserves_kAux`. -/
theorem contentEnd_preserves {k : K} {s : S3} {q i : Nat} (hk : KInv s)
    (hpre : ContentEndPre k s q i) : KInv (endUseEff s q) := by
  have hw := hk.1
  refine EndFree.releases_preserve hk (EndFree.endUseS_releases s q) rfl rfl rfl
    (fun q h => by simp only [endUseS, Bool.or_eq_false_iff] at h; exact h.1)
    (fun q' pl r hq hp => ?_) (fun q' _ x hx => ?_) (contentEnd_anchors hk.2.1.1.2.2.1 hpre)
    (fun r n z pr _ hur hz _ _ hpr hzh _ => ?_)
    (contentEnd_noDangling hw hk.2.1.2.2 hk.2.1.1.1 hpre)
  · obtain ⟨-, -, -, -, hd⟩ := hw.places q' pl r hq hp
    simp only [endUseS, hd, decide_eq_decide.2 (EndFree.ownedIn_parent hw hq hp)]
  · simp only [endUseS] at hx; split at hx
    · simp at hx
    · exact hx
  · have hnh : ¬ heldIn s.P q z.holder := fun hh => by
      have hd := EndFree.dead_false hur
      simp only [endUseS, Bool.or_eq_false_iff, decide_eq_false_iff_not] at hd
      rw [hzh] at hh
      cases ho : pr.owner with
      | frame f => rw [ho] at hh; exact hh
      | place o => rw [ho] at hh; exact hd.2 (.direct hpr ho hh)
    rw [EndFree.endUseS_get, hz]; simp [hnh]

/-- The end of the content of a slot place `q` preserves the auxiliary `KAux` (`RootHeldConv`, §40,
§49.7; not a clause of §57) (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3; §69 effect: places are unchanged and
authorities are only released). -/
theorem contentEnd_preserves_kAux {s : S3} {q : Nat} (ha : KAux s) : KAux (endUseEff s q) :=
  EndFree.releases_preserve_kAux ha (EndFree.endUseS_releases s q) rfl

/-! ## Kernel side of the pool operations (§57, §58; HandlePool v0.4 annex) -/

/-- Sequences of kernel steps compose (§57; HandlePool v0.4 annex). -/
theorem KSeq.trans {k : K} {s₁ s₂ s₃ : S3} (h₁ : KSeq k s₁ s₂) (h₂ : KSeq k s₂ s₃) :
    KSeq k s₁ s₃ := by
  induction h₂ with
  | refl => exact h₁
  | tail _ hs ih => exact .tail ih hs

/-- One kernel step is a sequence (§57; HandlePool v0.4 annex). -/
theorem KSeq.single {k : K} {s s' : S3} (h : KStep k s s') : KSeq k s s' := .tail (.refl s) h

/-- `releaseAll` is a sequence of `release` steps (§62; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2). -/
theorem releaseAll_kseq {k : K} : ∀ {s s' : S3} {l : List Nat}, releaseAll s l = some s' →

/-- The kernel state of every library-reachable state is reached from `S3.init statics` by kernel
steps O1–O16 and ends of slot contents (§57; HandlePool v0.4 annex), given `KInv` on such
states. -/
theorem pReach_xreach {k : K} {statics : Statics} (hX : KernelGuarantee k statics)
    {L : PState} (h : PReach k statics L) : XReach k statics L.kern := by
  induction h with
  | init => exact .init
  | step _ hs ih => exact xreach_pstep ih (hX _ ih) hs

/-- `KInv` (§57) together with the auxiliary `KAux` (§40, §49.7; not a clause of §57) holds on
every state reached by kernel steps and ends of slot contents, when it holds initially and every
kernel step O1–O16 preserves it (`contentEnd_preserves` and `contentEnd_preserves_kAux` cover the
ends of slot contents; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3). -/
theorem xreach_inv {k : K} {statics : Statics}
    (h0 : KInv (S3.init statics) ∧ KAux (S3.init statics))
    (hK : ∀ s s', KInv s → KAux s → KStep k s s' → KInv s' ∧ KAux s') {s : S3}
    (h : XReach k statics s) : KInv s ∧ KAux s := by
  induction h with
  | init => exact h0
  | step _ hs ih =>
    cases hs with
    | kernel hs => exact hK _ _ ih.1 ih.2 hs
    | contentEnd hpre => exact ⟨contentEnd_preserves ih.1 hpre, contentEnd_preserves_kAux ih.2⟩

/-! ## Helper lemmas (lists, chains, effects) -/

/-- An optional value satisfying a predicate with default `False` exists
(§38; HandlePool v0.4 annex). -/
theorem optP_false_iff {α : Type} {o : Option α} {P : α → Prop} :
    OptP o P False ↔ ∃ y, o = some y ∧ P y := by
        ⟨l, by simpa [S3.afp, hz] using hlz, hl⟩
      have := chain_lt hij
      unfold Exempt at hex'
      rcases hex' with rfl | h'
      · omega
      · have := chain_lt h'; omega
    rw [hnil, hmy]; rfl
  obtain ⟨l, hl⟩ := hok.slotLeaf q hq
  exact ⟨Arena.usable_of_covered hnd hy ya (hcov l hl) hl,
    ⟨pl.internal, List.mem_range.2 (lt_of_getElem? hy), hex,
      fun l hl => by rw [heff l hl]; exact Arena.allows_some_modify _⟩⟩

/-- An accepted `freeSlot` preserves the kernel invariant `KInv` (§57; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3:
"la correspondance des effets et la préservation des invariants sous ce droit constituent une
obligation explicite de reconstruction"); the auxiliary
`KAux` is preserved by `freeSlot_preserves_kAux`. -/
theorem freeSlot_preserves {k : K} {L L' : PState} {j : Nat} {h : Handle} (hk : KInv L.kern)
    (hst : FreeSlotStep k j h L (.ok L')) : KInv L'.kern := by
  obtain ⟨pl, sl, -, -, -, -, hpre, he, -⟩ := pool_freeSlot_ends_content hst
  rw [he]; exact contentEnd_preserves hk hpre

/-- An accepted `freeSlot` preserves the auxiliary `KAux` (`RootHeldConv`, §40, §49.7; not a clause
of §57) (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3; §69 effect). -/
theorem freeSlot_preserves_kAux {k : K} {L L' : PState} {j : Nat} {h : Handle}
    (ha : KAux L.kern) (hst : FreeSlotStep k j h L (.ok L')) : KAux L'.kern := by
  obtain ⟨pl, sl, -, -, -, -, -, he, -⟩ := pool_freeSlot_ends_content hst
  rw [he]; exact contentEnd_preserves_kAux ha

/-- `pool_freeSlot_ends_content` under the `Modify` right (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3): on a state
of a library run (`PReachI`) satisfying `KInv` (§57), an accepted `freeSlot` acts on a usable slot
over which the current frame has exercisable `Modify` through `internal` (§69.1), and leaves the
slot usable (§69: "`place` remains usable"; D.3: no deallocation). -/
theorem pool_freeSlot_under_modify {k : K} {statics : Statics} {L L' : PState}
    (hL : PReachI k statics L) (hk : KInv L.kern) {j : Nat} {h : Handle}
    (hst : FreeSlotStep k j h L (.ok L')) :
    ∃ pl sl, L.pools[j]? = some pl ∧ pl.slots[h.slot]? = some sl ∧
      L.kern.Usable sl.place ∧ HasRight L.kern .modify sl.place ∧
      L'.kern = endUseEff L.kern sl.place ∧ L'.kern.Usable sl.place := by
  obtain ⟨-, hwf, -⟩ := pReachI_inv hL
  obtain ⟨pl, sl, hp, hsl, hR, -, hpre, he, -⟩ := pool_freeSlot_ends_content hst
  have hpl : pl ∈ L.pools := List.mem_of_getElem? hp

86:theorem init_history {k : K} {statics : Statics} {s : S3} {l : Nat}
87:    (h : KStar k (S3.init statics) s) (hl : s.I l = .init) :
88:    (∃ e, statics[l]? = some e ∧ e.2 = true) ∨
89:      ∃ (t t' : S3) (op : KernelOp), KStar k (S3.init statics) t ∧ op.Step k t (.ok t') ∧
90:        t.I l ≠ .init ∧ t'.I l = .init ∧ op.Writes t l ∧ KStar k t' s := by
91:  induction h with
92:  | refl => exact .inl ((init_statics statics l).1 hl)
93:  | tail ht hst ih =>
94:    rename_i t u
95:    by_cases htl : t.I l = .init
96:    · rcases ih htl with hd | ⟨t₀, t₀', op, h₀, hs₀, hn₀, hi₀, hw₀, h₀'⟩
97:      · exact .inl hd
98:      · exact .inr ⟨t₀, t₀', op, h₀, hs₀, hn₀, hi₀, hw₀, .tail h₀' hst⟩
99:    · obtain ⟨op, hop⟩ := kstep_iff.1 hst
100:      exact .inr ⟨t, u, op, ht, hop, htl, hl, init_only_by_writes hop htl hl, .refl⟩

**DS-R1 "a cell above m" [draft].** DS-v1: "rejects if an active authority derived from internal
covers a cell above m". Reading: the cells at positions `[m.top, top)` (`above`), those that
`rewind m` returns. Alternative A: any cell at position `≥ m.top`. Alternative B: the regions issued
after `m`. Example (`Witness.reading_above`, decided): after `rewind ⟨0,1,1⟩` (top 1) and the
program's `release(5)`, `derive(4, [3], Modify)` gives authority 8, active, derived from `internal`
4, on cell 3 (position 1 ≥ `m0.top` = 0, but ≥ current top). `rewind ⟨0,0,0⟩` is `ok` here; under
A it is rejected. Safety is unaffected: the next `push` over cell 3 is rejected by the effective
right (§43, §61.1). Under B, a block grown after `m` from a base below `m` blocks `rewind` on its
lower part too (draft `opsE4`; not re-run here).

**DS-R2 order of the dead/foreign-mark `fail` and of the right of §36 [draft].** §58: "static
preconditions are checked before dynamic availability, according to the operation's contract";
DS-v1 lists "fails on a dead or foreign mark" first and says nothing about §36. Reading: mark
liveness first (`fail`), then `AdminRight` (`reject`). Alternative: §36 first. Example
(`Witness.reading_order` (1)): a callee frame with no right on the stack value rewinds to the
removed mark `⟨0,1,1⟩`: `fail` here, `reject` under the alternative. Consequence: `mark_no_aba`
gives `fail` unconditionally.

**DS-R4 `grow` with `extra = 0` [draft].** DS-v1 says nothing. Reading: `reject` ("grow" means a
larger size). Alternative: an in-place re-issue of the same region. Example
(`Witness.reading_order` (2)): `grow(0, 5, 0)` in `d9` is `reject`, while release, static checks,
in-place check, `split` and `store` of the same region are all `ok` (alternative: `ok`).

**DS-R5 `grow` of a live block that cannot extend in place: `fail`** (libs.md C10; DS-v1 "fail
otherwise"). The draft rejected it. Reading: the in-place check (`InPlace`: the block ends at the top
and `extra` cells follow) is the availability check of the derived issue (§77.4) and gives `fail`.
Example (`Witness.run_ok`): `grow(0, 5, 1)` in `d7`, where block 6 lies above block 5, is `fail`.
A `b` that is no block of the stack (`Stack.block` gives none): DS-v1 says nothing. Reading [draft

says nothing about creation. Reading: those of `newArena` other than its guard

# fix4-ds: B47, when `rewind` is `ok` (DS-v1, non-normative)

Files: `formal/Ern/Lib/DataStack.lean` (+281 lines, 0 removed) and `R/readings/datastack.md` (R3 rewritten, DS-R12 added, examples list updated). No commit was made.

## Contract text (brief.md obligation 6, verbatim)

"rewind m fails on a dead or foreign mark, rejects if an active authority derived from internal covers a cell above m, otherwise returns those cells to available and removes m and every mark above it"

## Result: both (a) and (b), as an exact characterization

`rewind_ok_iff` (DataStack.lean:660) states that on a library-reachable state with an existing stack, `rewind m` is `ok` iff the three conditions below hold:

```
theorem rewind_ok_iff {k : K} {statics : Statics} {D : DState} (hr : DReach k statics D)
    {j : Nat} {st : Stack} (hst : D.stacks[j]? = some st) {m : Mark} :
    (∃ D', RewindStep k j m D (.ok D')) ↔
      LiveMark j st m ∧ AdminRight D.kern st ∧
        ∀ (x l : Nat) (y : Authority), D.kern.A[x]? = some y → y.active = true →
          st.internal ∈ D.kern.ancs x → l ∈ y.footprint → l ∉ above st m
```

The hypotheses and conditions, with their sources:
- `DReach`: the library state invariant. It is the only invariant used: no `KInv`, no I3, no `KAux`.
- `LiveMark`: DS-v1, live and own mark.
- `AdminRight`: §36.
- The last conjunct: the DS-v1 condition, in the same form as the hypotheses of `rewind_rejects_live_above`.
- The model has no explicit check for that condition. It is the effective `Modify` of `internal` that `split` requires (§61.1, with the effective mode of §43). §61.3 follows from the same condition.

(b) `Witness.reading_rewind_right` (DataStack.lean:1279) is the counterexample. It is decided on `d16`, a `DReach K0 wst` state, and is recorded as DS-R12:
- In `d16`, mark `⟨0,0,0⟩` is live for stack 0, and no active authority derived from `internal` 4 covers cell 2 (`above st9 m0`).
- The current frame is a callee with no right on the stack value, so `¬ AdminRight`.
- `rewind` is `reject` and never `ok`.
- `split` of `internal` alone would also reject there (`¬ ExercisableAt 4 Modify`, §61.1).

The reason for this rejection is §36, which DS-v1 does not list. Under the reading "DS-v1's list is exhaustive" the outcome is `ok`.

## Declarations added (all additions, no existing statement changed)

All added declarations cite a § clause and "DS-v1, non-normative".
- `DBound` (:466): every anchor in `D` is an index of `A` (§44, §42).
- `kstep_dBound` (:471): each of the 16 kernel steps keeps `DBound`.
- `dBound_of_reachable` (:546): `DBound` holds on every kernel-reachable state.
- `StackShape` (:555): `internal` exists, has own mode `Modify` and covers every cell of the stack (§76.2, §76.3, §42).
- `DStep.akeep` (:562): a library step keeps the authorities.
- `stackShape_keep` (:583) and `set_keeps` (:595): helpers for the preservation proof.
- `DStep.stackShape` (:607) and `DReach.stackShape` (:631): `StackShape` is preserved by every library step and holds on every library-reachable state.
- `release_after_split` (:641): the `release` of the fresh `split` authority is accepted under `DBound` (§62).
- `rewind_ok_iff` (:660).
- `Witness.d16` (:1270) and `Witness.reading_rewind_right` (:1279).

None. No existing definition, theorem or hypothesis was touched; `git diff` shows 281 insertions and 0 deletions.

- The sorry/admit/native_decide/axiom grep prints nothing.

- It is not proved whether the explicit §36 check (`AdminRight`) ever rejects where the `split` check of §61.1 (`internal` active and exercisable at `Modify`) would accept. Noted in R3.
  - Likely no on `DReach`: `internal` stays held by a place, by §76.3 `heldByPlace` and `AKeep`'s `isPlace` clause, and parameters of §72 must be frame-held. Then `MetaRight` ↔ `ExercisableAt` as in `Arena.metaRight_iff`.

/-! ## Preservation by every step except `transfer` (§57, §58) -/

/-- Every operation other than `transfer` preserves `KInv` (§57) from its `ok` outcome, under
`DDSound` (§80, used by `split`, §61). -/
theorem op_preserves {k : K} {op : KernelOp} {s s' : S3} (hdd : DDSound k) (hinv : KInv s)
    (h : op.Step k s (.ok s')) (hnt : ∀ src dst, op ≠ .transfer src dst) : KInv s' := by
  cases op with
  | derive => exact derive_preserves hinv h
  | split => exact split_preserves hdd hinv h
  | release => exact release_preserves hinv h
  | transfer src dst => exact absurd rfl (hnt src dst)
  | depend => exact depend_preserves hinv h
  | enter => exact enter_preserves hinv h
  | exit => exact exit_preserves hinv h
  | read => exact read_preserves hinv h
  | write => exact write_preserves hinv h
  | writeShared => exact writeShared_preserves hinv h
  | pin => exact pin_preserves hinv h
  | unpin => exact unpin_preserves hinv h
  | endUse => exact endUse_preserves hinv h
  | free => exact free_preserves hinv h
  | alloc => exact alloc_preserves hinv h
  | store => exact store_preserves hinv h

/-- Every operation, `transfer` included, preserves the auxiliary `KAux` (`RootHeldConv`, §40,
§49.7; not a clause of §57) from a state satisfying `KInv` (§57) and `KAux` to its `ok`
outcome. -/
theorem op_preserves_kAux {k : K} {op : KernelOp} {s s' : S3} (hinv : KInv s) (haux : KAux s)
    (h : op.Step k s (.ok s')) : KAux s' := by
  cases op with
  | derive => exact derive_preserves_rootHeldConv haux h
  | split => exact split_preserves_rootHeldConv haux h
  | release => exact release_preserves_rootHeldConv haux h
  | transfer => exact transfer_preserves_kAux haux h
  | depend => exact depend_preserves_rootHeldConv haux h
  | enter => exact enter_preserves_kAux hinv haux h
  | exit => exact exit_preserves_kAux haux h
  | read => exact read_preserves_kAux haux h
  | write => exact write_preserves_kAux haux h
  | writeShared => exact writeShared_preserves_kAux haux h
  | pin => exact pin_preserves_kAux haux h
  | unpin => exact unpin_preserves_kAux haux h
  | endUse => exact endUse_preserves_kAux haux h
  | free => exact free_preserves_kAux haux h
  | alloc => exact alloc_preserves_kAux hinv haux h
  | store => exact store_preserves_rootHeldConv haux h

/-- Every kernel step from a state satisfying `KInv` (§57) under `DDSound` (§80) either preserves
`KInv` or is an accepted `transfer` (§63), the one exception (`transfer_breaks_kinv`). -/
theorem kstep_preserves {k : K} {s s' : S3} (hdd : DDSound k) (hinv : KInv s)
    (h : KStep k s s') : KInv s' ∨ ∃ src dst, TransferStep k src dst s (.ok s') := by
  obtain ⟨op, hop⟩ := kstep_iff.1 h
  cases op with
  | transfer src dst => exact .inr ⟨src, dst, hop⟩
  | _ => exact .inl (op_preserves hdd hinv hop fun _ _ e => KernelOp.noConfusion e)

/-- Every kernel step preserves the auxiliary `KAux` (§40, §49.7) from a state satisfying `KInv`
(§57) and `KAux`. -/
theorem kstep_preserves_kAux {k : K} {s s' : S3} (hinv : KInv s) (haux : KAux s)
    (h : KStep k s s') : KAux s' := by
  obtain ⟨op, hop⟩ := kstep_iff.1 h
  exact op_preserves_kAux hinv haux hop

/-- `mark_no_aba` (DS-v1, non-normative: marks carry a fresh identifier; `rewind m` removes `m` and
every mark above it): every mark removed by an `ok` of `rewind m`, `m` and every later mark of the
stack, is live in no stack after any later run, even when the top returns to its position, and its
`rewind` fails, with no other outcome (§58), on every existing stack. Under `MarksWF`, which holds
on every library-reachable state (`DReach.marksWF`). -/
theorem mark_no_aba {k : K} {D D₁ D' : DState} {j : Nat} {m : Mark} (hw : MarksWF D)
    (hr : RewindStep k j m D (.ok D₁)) (hrun : DRun k D₁ D') {st : Stack}
    (hst : D.stacks[j]? = some st) {pre post : List Mark} (hs : st.marks = pre ++ m :: post)
    {m' : Mark} (hm' : m' ∈ m :: post) :
    (∀ (i : Nat) (st' : Stack), D'.stacks[i]? = some st' → m' ∉ st'.marks) ∧
      ∀ (i : Nat) (st' : Stack), D'.stacks[i]? = some st' →
        RewindStep k i m' D' .fail ∧ ∀ o, RewindStep k i m' D' o → o = .fail := by
  obtain ⟨hnd, hms⟩ := hw j st hst
  rw [hs] at hnd
  · simp only [Refinement.leafAcc, heq, ↓reduceIte]

/-- `grow_keeps_prefix_bytes` (DS-v1, non-normative; through the refinement of Part XVII, §82): an
`ok` of `grow b extra` is the kernel steps `release(b)`, `split(internal, [region])` and
`store(|A|, dst)`; their realization in the memory machine (`Refinement.opsOf`) has no raw
operation for `release` and `split` (§62, §61), and the raw operations of `store` (one write into
the range of the destination, §82.3) leave the bytes, values and provenances, of every cell of the
old block unchanged, for every layout satisfying the layout interface `LayoutWF` (§82.1, §23) in
the state before the step. -/
theorem grow_keeps_prefix_bytes {Ty : Type} {k : K} {D D' : DState} {j b extra : Nat}
    (h : GrowStep k j b extra D (.ok D')) {st : Stack} {x : Blk} (hst : D.stacks[j]? = some st)
    (hx : st.block b = some x) :
    ∃ s₁ s₂, Refinement.OpStep k (.release b) D.kern s₁ ∧
      Refinement.OpStep k (.split st.internal [cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)]) s₁ s₂ ∧
      Refinement.OpStep k (.store D.kern.A.length x.dst) s₂ D'.kern ∧
      ∀ (π : Refinement.Params Ty) (s2 : Machine.State), Refinement.LayoutWF π.L D.kern s2 →
        Refinement.opsOf π (.release b) D.kern s2 = [] ∧
        Refinement.opsOf π (.split st.internal [cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)]) s₁ s2 = [] ∧
        ∀ l ∈ cellsOf st x.base x.size, ∀ i < (π.L l).len,
          Refinement.bytesOf
            (Refinement.run s2 (Refinement.opsOf π (.store D.kern.A.length x.dst) s₂ s2)) π.L l i =
          Refinement.bytesOf s2 π.L l i := by
  cases h with
  | @ok st₀ x₀ s₁ s₂ s₃ hst₀ hx₀ hpos hrl hstat hin hsp hsto =>
    rw [hst] at hst₀; cases hst₀; rw [hx] at hx₀; cases hx₀

/-! ## No dangling authority after the exit (§73, §54) -/

/-- `exitFrame_no_dangling` (§73, §54): from a state satisfying `WF3` (§49), `I1` (§50) and
`NoDangling` (§54), clauses of §57, after an `ok` exit no active authority covers a leaf of a
place that is not usable, in particular of a local of the exited frame or of storage dying with

theorem exitFrame_no_dangling {k : K} {s s' : S3} (hw : WF3 s) (h1 : I1 s) (hnd : NoDangling s)

    ∀ q, ¬ s'.Usable q → ∀ (j : Nat) (y : Authority), s'.A[j]? = some y → y.active = true →

a state violating `KInv` (holder validity §49.8 and `NoDangling` §54 fail,
`cyc3_not_wf3_noDangling`). -/
theorem transfer_breaks_kinv : DDSound Examples.K0 ∧ ∃ s s', Reachable Examples.K0 cycStatics s ∧
    KInv s ∧ KAux s ∧ TransferStep Examples.K0 0 3 s (.ok s') ∧ ¬ KInv s' :=
  ⟨fun _ _ h => (h : False).elim, cyc2, cyc3, cyc2_reachable, cyc2_kInv.1, cyc2_kInv.2,
    cyc2_transfer, fun h => cyc3_not_wf3_noDangling.1 h.1⟩

/-! ## The destination's usability does not suffice (§44, §63.7)

§63.7 checks `AnchorOrderHeld` only for the moved held authorities. In `ahx`, the derived
authority 6 is held by place 2, outside the transferred value, without being among its anchors
(`HeldAnchored` fails), and its effective anchor, the root 3 held by the source, moves with the
/-! ## Reachable states (§57) -/

/-- §57 as stated is false: under a contract satisfying `DDSound` (§80) and well-formed statics
(§47), a reachable state violates `KInv`, after an accepted `transfer` (§63,
`transfer_breaks_kinv`). -/
theorem reachable_kinv_false : ¬ ∀ (k : K) (statics : Statics) (s : S3), DDSound k →
    StaticsOK statics → Reachable k statics s → KInv s := by
  intro hall
  obtain ⟨hdd, s, s', hr, -, -, ht, hn⟩ := transfer_breaks_kinv
  exact hn (hall _ _ _ hdd (by decide) (.step hr (.transfer ht)))

**Q23. All recorded readings, submitted as the policy requires.**
- `R/readings/kernel-defs.md`: B#1–B#47 and SP-A1–SP-A5. Verdict-changing examples:
  - B#1, §43 one authority over all leaves (∃∀): `split(root S, [[f1],[f2]])` then `pin(S)` is `reject` under ∃∀ and `ok` under ∀∃;
  - B#15, §62.3: W4, `split(a, [[]])` then `release(a)` is `reject` or `ok`;
  - B#28, §69.2 qualifier dropped: W3 (`kd_Readings.lean`:28-34), `endUse` through a `Modify` parameter is `reject` or `ok`;
  - B#33, §70.4 scope;
  - B#45, per-leaf pin flags: `pin(S); pin(f1); unpin(f1); transfer(f1, d)` is `ok` or `reject`;
  - SP-A4, the domain of `StaticPinnedBottom`;
  - B#39, provider usability: its recorded consequence "none on states with `NoDangling`" is false (Q24, B46).
- `R/readings/handlepool.md` H-R1–H-R11 (H-R5 is the scope of the exemption).
- `R/readings/datastack.md` DS-R1–DS-R13, including the missing-stack case of DS-R3 (`RewindStep.noStack`, DataStack.lean:218: `reject` here, `fail` if the mark counts as dead or foreign; `R/final5/nostack.lean`).
- `R/readings/arena.md` A-R766.
- `R/readings/machine.md` S1 (§15.3, "required" bytes) and S2 (byte read vs typed read).
- Also to settle: B44 (definitions of the clauses with no checkable content). B43 (DESIGN.md step function vs §20.1 relations) is a DESIGN.md wording question for its owner, not a spec question (note under the table of section 1).

**Q24. §71.2: existence of the provider (B46; round 0, ops-b F1).**
- Passage: §71.2, "All leaves of the provider are `Init`; updates to its metadata are permitted through exercisable `Modify` or a valid `writeShared` over `SharedMutable` metadata". It does not say that the provider is a place.
- Readings: no existence condition (current: the footprint of a non-place is empty, so both conditions hold vacuously); or the draft clause `Usable provider`.
- Program: from `S3.init [((none, none, 0), true)]`, which satisfies `NoDangling`, `alloc` with provider 5. It is `ok` as the model stands and `reject` with `Usable provider`.
- Witness: `R/report-check/records/b39.lean`, `B39.b39`. `R/readings/kernel-defs.md` B#39's "none on states with `NoDangling`" is false.

**Q25. §69.2: is `place` among "the places dying with `place`"? (round 0, ops-b F3).**
- Passage: §69.2 exempts only derivatives held by "the places dying with `place`". The §69 effect says "`place` remains usable as a place".
- Readings: (a) strict literal: an authority held by the surviving `place` blocks `endUse`; (b) `place`, whose value dies, counts among the dying places (current: `Access.EndUseAccessOK`, Ops.lean:709, exempts every authority held within `place`). The mixed reading actually used is recorded in neither `R/readings/kernel-defs.md` B#28 nor B#29.
- Program: `R/report-check/records/V_r0.lean`:54-71, from the statics of `Access.Examples`: `alloc` (provider 0, owner 1) makes place 3; `derive(3, [3], Modify)` gives authority 4; `store(4, 0)`; `transfer(0, 1)`; then `endUse(1)` while authority 4 is held by place 1, which survives. It is `ok` under (b) (`EndUsePre K0 sd 1`) and `reject` under (a) (`EndUseAccessOK sd 1 4 ∧ ¬ StrictAccessOK sd 1 4`).

**Q26. §60.1 "its origin chain and anchors are valid", read through §44 (round 0, ops-a R1; linked to Q9).**
- Passage: §60.1. §44 gives "valid" a meaning: an anchor is valid while the authority it names is active. `R/readings/kernel-defs.md` SP-A5 and the policy record the clause as having no checkable content; round 0 (ops-a R1) found that record misdescribed.
- Readings: valid means "exists" (the clause is then redundant with WF3.5, and omitting it, as the model does, changes nothing) or "active" (as in Q9).
- Program: `R/report-check/records/r60.lean`: after the W2 run of Q9, `derive(3, [0], Observe)`, whose origin 2 is inactive. It is `ok` under "exists" (current, `R60.r60`) and `reject` under "active".

**Q27. DS-v1 `rewind`: does §36 add a reason to reject? (DS-R12; contract DS-v1, non-normative; B47 note in section 1).**
- Passages: DS-v1, "rewind m fails on a dead or foreign mark, rejects if an active authority derived from internal covers a cell above m, otherwise returns those cells to available and removes m and every mark above it". It names one reason to reject. §36, "For every administrative abstraction, including arenas, `HandlePool`, and `DataStack`, **`MetaRight` requires `Modify` exercisable on the administering value**", and "These abstractions remain libraries and add no rights to the kernel".
- Readings: (a) §36 applies, so `rewind` also rejects without `AdminRight` (current). For an existing stack this is the only reason outside DS-v1's list (`Lib.DataStack.rewind_ok_iff`, DataStack.lean:661). (b) DS-v1's list is exhaustive, so `rewind` is `ok` whenever the mark is live and no active authority derived from `internal` covers a cell above it.
- Program: `Lib.DataStack.Witness.reading_rewind_right` (:1280), state `d16` (:1271). After the rewind to `⟨0,1,1⟩` and the program's `release(5)`, a callee frame with no parameter or local is entered. Mark `⟨0,0,0⟩` is live for stack 0, and no active authority derived from `internal` 4 covers cell 2, the cell above it. `rewind ⟨0,0,0⟩` is `reject` under (a) and `ok` under (b). The kernel sequence cannot realize (b) there: `split` of `internal` also rejects, because `internal` is not exercisable at `Modify` (§61.1).
- Scope: existing stacks. A stack index with no stack gives `reject` through `RewindStep.noStack` (DataStack.lean:218), a further reason outside DS-v1's list (DS-R3, `R/final5/nostack.lean`; submitted with Q23).

**Q28. DS-v1 `rewind` on a live mark of a dead stack (DS-R13; contract DS-v1, non-normative; narrow check ds4-3).**
